body.x: INTERPOL is the world’s largest international police organization, with 196 Member Countries. Created in 1923, it facilitates cross-border police co-operation, and supports and assists all organizations, authorities, and services whose mission is to prevent or combat international crime.

INTERPOL actively encourages applications from women and nationals of member countries that are currently unrepresented among our staff (please click on this link to access the list of countries). Candidates from these countries are particularly encouraged to apply.
INTERPOL’s recruitment process is merit-based hence all hiring decisions are made considering the applicant’s qualifications and the needs of the Organization.
Job Title: Procurement & Budget Coordination Officer, BER
Reporting To: Senior Project Manager, INTERPOL Building Extension and Renovation Programme

Only professional experience for which candidates can provide official proof of employment will be considered. Candidates could be requested to provide copies of such official documents prior to interviews/test.
* Subsequent extension to this post will be subject to the terms of the Organization’s Staff Manual, to satisfactory performance and to availability of funds.

Tests/interviews in connection to this selection procedure will tentatively take place between 09 December 2026 and 17 December 2026. Applicants are kindly requested to plan their availability during this period accordingly in case they are short-listed.
Selected candidates will be expected to report for duty as soon as possible after receiving an offer of employment.
This selection exercise may be used to generate a reserve list of suitable candidates that may be used to address Organization's similar staffing needs in the future.

The Executive Directorate Resource Management (EDRM) enables INTERPOL’s global mission through the effective management of its financial, human, and corporate resources. Within EDRM, Buildings – Global Facilities is responsible for creating and managing secure, modern, and fit-for-purpose facilities across the Organization, including the delivery of the Lyon Headquarters Building Extension and Renovation Programme. Reporting to the Senior Project Manager, the Procurement and Budget Coordination Officer play an important role in enabling the successful delivery of the Programme. The Officer coordinates budget planning and monitoring, procurement activities, and financial reporting, ensuring that resources, processes, and information are effectively managed.

Working across project teams, Finance, Procurement, vendors and management, the role helps drive efficient delivery, strong coordination, and sound financial and procurement management throughout the Programme.

The Executive Directorate Resource Management (EDRM) enables INTERPOL’s global mission through the effective management of its financial, human, and corporate resources. Within EDRM, Buildings – Global Facilities is responsible for creating and managing secure, modern, and fit-for-purpose facilities across the Organization, including the delivery of the Lyon Headquarters Building Extension and Renovation Programme. Reporting to the Senior Project Manager, the Procurement and Budget Coordination Officer play an important role in enabling the successful delivery of the Programme. The Officer coordinates budget planning and monitoring, procurement activities, and financial reporting, ensuring that resources, processes, and information are effectively managed.

Working across project teams, Finance, Procurement, vendors and management, the role helps drive efficient delivery, strong coordination, and sound financial and procurement management throughout the Programme.
Support the preparation of annual and multi-year budget plans.
Coordinate budget submissions for the Building Programme.
Monitor budget execution and expenditure trends.
Prepare budget forecasts and identify potential funding gaps or surpluses.
Track commitments, obligations, and actual expenditures.
Ensure budget allocations are aligned with approved priorities and work plans.
Support budget revisions, transfers, and reallocations when required.
Prepare periodic budget and financial performance reports.
Develop dashboards and management reports highlighting financial status and trends.
Analyse variances between planned and actual expenditures and propose corrective actions.
Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation.
Provide management with accurate financial information to support strategic decisions.
Coordinate procurement planning activities with project managers and budget holders.
Consolidate procurement requirements and develop procurement schedules.
Prepare procurement requests and supporting documentation.
Liaise with procurement services throughout the procurement lifecycle.
Monitor procurement actions and contract implementation.
Track delivery timelines and ensure timely receipt of goods and services.
Maintain procurement records and reporting tools.
Monitor contract utilization and expenditure against approved budgets.
Coordinate contract renewals, amendments, and extensions.
Support vendor performance monitoring and issue resolution.
Ensure contract-related deliverables are properly documented and tracked.
Maintain an overview of contract obligations and key milestones.
Ensure compliance with applicable financial, procurement, and administrative rules.
Verify the availability of budget before initiating procurement activities.
Contribute to the implementation of internal control measures.
Support audits by providing required financial and procurement documentation.
Assist in addressing audit recommendations and implementing corrective actions.
Act as the focal point between operational teams, finance services, procurement services, and vendors.
Provide guidance to managers and project teams on budget and procurement procedures.
Facilitate coordination meetings and follow-up on agreed actions.
Promote best practices in budget management and procurement planning.
Support change management and process improvement initiatives.
Identify financial and procurement risks that may impact project delivery.
Develop mitigation measures and escalation plans.
Monitor critical procurement lead times and budget consumption rates.
Alert management to emerging risks affecting operational objectives.
Perform any other duty as required by the hierarchy.

Three to four years completed University degree or equivalent level of diploma, in a subject close to Business administration, Finance, Information technology, Process Management, Engineering or another relevant field.
A master’s degree in a relevant domain would be an asset.
Minimum three years’ experience in a relevant area. Ten years' experience in the area is required if the post holder does not have the required level of education.
A good level of written French is highly desirable.
Knowledge of other official languages of the Organization (Arabic, Spanish) is an asset.
Expert user of Excel, with exceptional aptitude for handling figures, data analysis, and reporting.
Proficiency in other Microsoft Office tools (Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Project and OneDrive).
Working knowledge of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems (e.g., SAP) is an asset.
Demonstrated high level of rigor and an excellent capacity for analysis and synthesis.
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to maintain objectivity and apply logical reasoning
Ability to work in teams as well as independently
Ability to effectively coordinate across multiple teams and consolidate diverse data sources.
Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple tasks and deadlines
Good interpersonal skills, particularly in a multicultural environment
Ability to develop and maintain professional networks
As part of our commitment to transparency throughout our recruitment process, INTERPOL's Staff Manual Regulation 11.4: Age-limit, which states that:

'Officials of the Organization shall not normally be retained in service beyond the age of 65 years. The Secretary General may, in exceptional cases and in the interests of the Organization, extend this age limit, in which case he shall inform the official concerned sufficiently in advance.'

Given this Regulation and in case candidates reach the age of 65 during the potential duration of the appointment, should they be selected for the position and the process proceed to appointment, the employment period may be affected by this regulatory limit and may therefore not extend for the full standard contract duration as published in the vacancy notice.
We are sharing this information to ensure transparency at this stage of the process.
This position is no longer open.
